Definition: of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian:--Crispus.
BiblicalUsage: Crispus was the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, and he believed on the Lord with all his house in Acts 18:8. Paul adds in 1 Corinthians 1:14 that he baptized Crispus himself, one of the very few he baptized at Corinth.
TheologicalSignificance: What convinces me here is that Crispus is the proof that no position is too high or too opposed for the gospel: the ruler of the synagogue believed, and his whole house with him.
